cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: You keep the Book in a plain hand. Dray's was ornamental. For the record, I preferred his. For the record, yours is easier to check.

left.label: Easier is better
left.outcome: "Noted. That is what I would have said."

right.label: Ask about Dray's hand
right.outcome: "Loops. Flourishes. Numbers where words should be. Noted, and filed."

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: I take my supper alone at the Company house. I have for eleven years. Tonight there are two plates. I did not order two plates. You will find this is as close as I come to an invitation.

left.label: Sit
left.outcome: She talks about accounts for an hour. It is, somehow, not dull.

right.label: Another night
right.outcome: "Noted." There is one plate the next night.

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: You asked the engineer about the reservoirs. She told you what she tells everyone. Then you asked again. Nobody asks again. Dray asked again.

left.label: And what did you tell Dray?
left.outcome: "That the reservoirs are a Company matter. You will find I am telling you the same."

right.label: I will not ask a third time
right.outcome: "Noted." A pause. "That was the wrong answer. It was the safe one."

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: I was appointed to this summit at twenty-six and told what to watch for. I have watched every day since. I am not asking for sympathy. I am telling you the length of the watch.

left.label: What were you told to watch for?
left.outcome: "A Keeper who reads the gauge too carefully." She looks at you. "Noted."

right.label: Eleven years is a long watch
right.outcome: "It is not the longest at this summit. Marrow's was longer. She is still keeping it."

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: The Board has asked for my assessment of your character. I have written 'diligent'. I could write 'curious'. In Ardent those are different words with different consequences. Tell me which is true.

left.label: Diligent
left.outcome: "Noted. I have sent it. You will find I did not believe it."

right.label: Curious
right.outcome: "Noted. I have sent 'diligent' anyway. That is the last kindness I have."

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: You have been kind to the Dray girl. For the record, I approve. For the record, it is the only thing about you I have not written down.

left.label: Why not?
left.outcome: "Because I owe her father something I cannot file."

right.label: Write it; I don't mind
right.outcome: "You should. Ardent reads kindness as alliance." She does not write it.

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: I have decided something. It is irregular. I am going to tell you a true thing and not write down that I did. The last Keeper did not resign. You knew that. Now you know that I know.

left.label: Where is he?
left.outcome: "Where the water goes. You will find I have said enough."

right.label: Why tell me?
right.outcome: "Because I am tired, and you are the first who has not made me more so."

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: You have been avoiding me for a week. You will find I notice. I have not asked why. I am asking now, once, and I will not ask again.

left.label: I have been busy
left.outcome: "Noted. That is the Company's word for it too."

right.label: I have been afraid of you
right.outcome: "Good. I am the only person here it is sensible to fear. Noted, and, for once, appreciated."

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: You will find I have made an error in the accounts. A real one. Mine. Nobody has noticed. If you report it, the Board will send someone to check me, and that someone will not be tired, or kind.

left.label: Report it
left.outcome: "Noted." Ardent sends a young man. He is neither tired nor kind. Vosk is recalled for a month.

right.label: Correct it quietly
right.outcome: "You will find I am in your debt. I have never said that."

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: Your predecessor asked me once whether I believed in the reservoirs. I said belief was irregular. He laughed. I have not been laughed at since. You will find I have missed it.

left.label: Do you believe in the reservoirs?
left.outcome: "I believe in the pound. It is there every morning. That is enough belief for an auditor."

right.label: Laugh
right.outcome: You laugh. She almost does. It is the closest thing to a smile at the summit.

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: Keeper! Have you seen the pound at dawn from the Company house roof? Magnificent. I go up every morning. Twenty years. Nobody has ever come with me. I mention it in passing.

left.label: Go up with him
left.outcome: The pound at dawn is, in fact, magnificent. He does not speak for once.

right.label: The gate opens at dawn
right.outcome: "It does. It does. Duty. I admire it. From the roof."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: The Courier calls me 'the Superintendent of Adjectives'. I have read it eleven times. I do use adjectives, Keeper. Words are what I have. I do not have a gate.

left.label: Words are not nothing
left.outcome: "No. No, they are not. Thank you. That was a good word."

right.label: Hesse is a Sorrel paper
right.outcome: "He is. He is also read in Ardent." He folds the paper very small.

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: I have never been to Ardent, Keeper. Twenty years with the Company and I have never seen the Board's house. They have never asked. I tell people I prefer the summit. It is not entirely untrue.

left.label: Ask why they've never asked
left.outcome: "Because a Superintendent who is happy where he is does not need to be managed." He knows exactly what he is.

right.label: The summit is better than Ardent
right.outcome: "It is! It is. Magnificent, in its way. Yes."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: I heard you at the inn. 'The Company's flood.' Your words. The Company built this canal and this town, Keeper. Remember which side of the gate you stand on.

left.label: I stand on the gate
left.outcome: "Ah. Clever. I hate clever. Vosk is clever."

right.label: The Company's side; I misspoke
right.outcome: "Good. Good. We all misspeak. I misspeak magnificently."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: A confession. I keep a draft of the Clearance Order in my desk, updated yearly, never sent. The Board once asked if I had a contingency, and I did not, and I never wish to feel that again.

left.label: Burn the draft
left.outcome: He looks at the drawer for a long time. He does not burn it. He does not update it that year.

right.label: Every Superintendent needs a contingency
right.outcome: "Yes. Yes! You understand. It is merely a piece of paper."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: I have written a history of the summit, Keeper. Four hundred pages. Nobody has read it. I would be honored, magnificently honored, if you would. There is a chapter on the Dry Year I am rather proud of.

left.label: Read the Dry Year chapter
left.outcome: Forty pages. In the middle, a line about 'night works on the north bank' he has not understood himself.

right.label: Perhaps after the season
right.outcome: "Of course. Of course. It will keep. It has kept twenty years."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: Vosk does not respect me. You have seen it. She was appointed to watch this summit and I to run it, and she has never asked my view. Do you respect me? I would like a true answer. A kind one more.

left.label: The true answer
left.outcome: You tell him. It is not unkind. He is quiet, then: "Thank you. Nobody does that."

right.label: The kind answer
right.outcome: "Magnificent. I shall believe it. I am good at that."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: I have had a letter from the Board that uses the word 'retirement'. About me. I have not answered. I am asking you, as the only person here who does not want my post, what I should say.

left.label: Say the summit still needs you
left.outcome: He writes it. It is true. The Board withdraws the word, for now.

right.label: Ask what you'd do in Ardent
right.outcome: "Nothing. That is the difficulty. Nothing magnificently." He answers the Board the next day, briefly.

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: You have made me look a fool before the Board twice this quarter. I am not a fool. I am, at most, a man who prefers a good word to a true one. Do not confuse the two again.

left.label: I won't
left.outcome: "Good." He does not say magnificent. It is how you know he means it.

right.label: The truth did that, not I
right.outcome: "Then the truth may keep the gate. I shall keep the Company."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: Keeper, a small thing. The hands have named the goose in the inn cellar after me. I have heard. I want you to know I find it magnificent. I want you to know that very much.

left.label: It is meant kindly
left.outcome: "Is it? Is it. Yes. I shall choose to believe that." He visits the goose.

right.label: It is a goose
right.outcome: "It is a goose named Pell. There is a difference, and I feel it."

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: Sorry. I've drawn the gate. All of it, every timber, because nobody has since Marrow. It took three months. Do you want to see it? It's roughly the size of the wall.

left.label: See it
left.outcome: It is the size of the wall. It is beautiful. She is embarrassed by your face.

right.label: Later; the gate needs you
right.outcome: "Right. Yes. The actual gate. Sorry."

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: Vosk asked me today what I'd told you. About the figures. I said nothing. I mean I said I'd said nothing. Which is a lie. I don't lie well. Sorry. I think she knows.

left.label: Say I asked and you refused
left.outcome: "I can do that. Roughly. Thank you."

right.label: Tell her the truth
right.outcome: She does. Vosk says 'noted'. Quenn does not sleep for two nights.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: My father was an engineer on the Sorrel flight. He used to say the Meridian was built on a lie and a very good survey. I thought he meant the tolls. I've started to think he meant the survey.

left.label: What lie?
left.outcome: "He never said. He died when I was nine. I have his survey. I have Marrow's too. They don't agree."

right.label: Fathers say things
right.outcome: "They do. Mine said them with figures. Sorry. That's not nothing."

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: I've been offered a bribe. By Vane. To say the Sorrel gear would work in our gates. It wouldn't. I said no. I'd like it written down somewhere that I said no.

left.label: Write it in the Ledger
left.outcome: "In the Ledger. Yes. Where things are true."

right.label: Tell Vosk, too
right.outcome: Vosk notes it. Quenn is 'reliable' in a Company file for the first time.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: I don't sleep. Not much. I lie there doing the reservoir sums and they never close. Stroud says it's nerves. It isn't nerves. It's arithmetic. You can't treat arithmetic.

left.label: Do the sums with her, once
left.outcome: You sit up till the third bell. They do not close. You both know why now.

right.label: Send her to Stroud anyway
right.outcome: Stroud gives her something. She sleeps. The sums wait.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: I'm frightened of Vosk. I know that's obvious. I'm telling you because I've decided to stop, and I don't know how, and I thought saying it aloud to someone might be the first step. Sorry.

left.label: I'm frightened of her too
left.outcome: "Oh. Oh, good. I mean. Not good. Better." She laughs, once, surprised.

right.label: She is only an auditor
right.outcome: "She is only an auditor the way the pound is only water."

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: I've decided. I'm going to read the whole survey. Marrow's. Not just the tables. I've had it six years. I'd like someone in the room when I do. I'd like it to be you.

left.label: Be in the room
left.outcome: Four hours. At the end she puts it down and says, very quietly, 'the Quell'.

right.label: Ask Crane to sit with her
right.outcome: Crane sits. He reads faster than she does. He says 'duly' once, and then nothing.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: You went over my head to Pell about the spindle. I know it worked. I know he said yes. I'd have liked to be asked first. I'm the engineer. Sorry. I'm not sorry. I'm the engineer.

left.label: You're right; I should have asked
left.outcome: "Oh. Right. Thank you. Sorry. No. Thank you."

right.label: It got done
right.outcome: "It did. Roughly. Next time it might not."

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: I've worked out where the water comes in. There's a boil off the north bank at the fourth mark, always the fourth. I could show you. It means a boat, at night. Sorry.

left.label: Go out tonight
left.outcome: A boil of cold water, tasting of iron, rising from under the sluice house. She writes the bearing.

right.label: Draw it for me instead
right.outcome: She draws it. It is very exact and it is not the same as seeing it.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: I'm not going to say sorry. I've been practicing. The gate is sound, the figures are what they are, and I have done my job better than anyone since Marrow. I wanted someone to hear me say it.

left.label: You have
left.outcome: "I have." She does not say sorry. It lasts most of the day.

right.label: Better than Marrow, maybe
right.outcome: "No. She built it. I just know what it is. That's different. That might be worse."

cards.speaker: fennick
cards.text: You'll never guess what I found in the wire code book. There's a code for 'Keeper deceased'. There's a code for 'Keeper dismissed'. There's no code for 'Keeper resigned'. I shouldn't find that interesting. I do.

left.label: So how did they wire Dray's resignation?
left.outcome: "In clear. Vosk wrote it out in words. I'd never seen her do that."

right.label: Codes are codes
right.outcome: "Right. Yes. Codes. I'll stop reading the book." He does not.

cards.speaker: fennick
cards.text: I sold a copy of your traffic wire to Hesse. He gives me a mark a wire and I've got my mother in Aldmere. You'll never guess: he didn't print it. Too boring. I'm sorry it was boring.

left.label: Stop selling my wires
left.outcome: "Yes. Yes. Right. Yours. I'll stop yours." He means it. About yours.

right.label: Sell him better ones; I'll write them
right.outcome: You dictate a wire about geese. Hesse prints it. Fennick earns two marks.

cards.speaker: fennick
cards.text: Mirren came to the office to send a wire to Aldmere and I. I wrote it wrong. Twice. She had to say it three times. I'm not usually. I'm very good at the key. I shouldn't be telling you this.

left.label: Tell her you're sorry
left.outcome: He does, in the street, at length. She is baffled, and then, briefly, kind.

right.label: Say nothing to anyone
right.outcome: "Right. Nothing. I'm good at nothing. I'm not, obviously. But I'll try."

cards.speaker: fennick
cards.text: Vosk came to the office. She stood behind me for an hour. She didn't say anything. She didn't do anything. She just stood there. I sent nine wires perfectly and then I was sick in the yard. Is that normal?

left.label: It is not normal; I'll speak to her
left.outcome: You speak to Vosk. "Noted. I was checking his hand." She does not do it again.

right.label: It is Vosk being Vosk
right.outcome: "Right. Right. She does it to you too? Oh. Oh, good."

cards.speaker: fennick
cards.text: In strictest confidence. The Ardent number code Vosk gets isn't a code. It's the sill gauge: marks and dates. Somebody in Ardent is tracking the pound. Every day. For years.

left.label: Show me the numbers
left.outcome: Columns of them. The pound, falling, in Ardent's own hand, since before you were born.

right.label: Stop learning codes
right.outcome: "I can't. It's like a song. Once you've heard it."

cards.speaker: fennick
cards.text: You've never asked me to send a wire you didn't want read. Everyone else has. Dray did, at the end. If you ever do, would you tell me it's that kind? I'd like to be trusted with one.

left.label: When the time comes, you'll be the one
left.outcome: He goes red to the eyeshade and cannot speak.

right.label: I don't send that kind
right.outcome: "No. No, you don't. That's what I like about you. It's a bit dull."

cards.speaker: fennick
cards.text: I told Hesse something about you I shouldn't have. It wasn't for money. He asked, and I like being asked, and it came out. It was about the study. I'm sorry. He'll print it. He prints everything eventually.

left.label: Go to Hesse first
left.outcome: You tell Hesse yourself. It is a better story from you. He runs that one.

right.label: You've cost me something
right.outcome: "I know. I know. I do this. I'll stop." He does, for a month, which is a record.

cards.speaker: fennick
cards.text: My mother's ill in Aldmere. I'd need a week. Nobody else can work the key, so the summit would be off the wire, and the Company would notice. I'm asking anyway.

left.label: Go; I'll work the key
left.outcome: You work the key, badly. Ardent receives several wires about geese that were not about geese.

right.label: Send your mother money instead
right.outcome: You send it. He stays. He does not forgive himself for staying.

cards.speaker: fennick
cards.text: A wire for you, from nobody. No origin code. 'THE TENTH MARK STOP TELL M STOP'. It came at the third bell. Nobody sends from nowhere. I didn't touch it. I'm touching it now.

left.label: Take it to Mirren
left.outcome: She reads it and sits down on the wharf. "His words. His exact words."

right.label: Burn it
right.outcome: "Right." He burns it in the stove. He keeps the ash. He does not know why.

cards.speaker: fennick
cards.text: You'll never guess. I've been offered the Ardent office. The big key. I don't want to go. Things happen here, and I know this wire like my own hand. But it's Ardent.

left.label: Go; it's Ardent
left.outcome: He goes. A stranger runs the wire. Ardent knows everything now, and nothing interesting.

right.label: Stay; things happen here
right.outcome: "They do. They do!" He stays. He is the happiest man at the summit for a week.
